avoid_for: Any context needing multiple colors, imagery, or hierarchy beyond type — software dashboards, e-commerce catalogues, corporate sites, or playful multi-color brands; the two-color band system and 288px type leave no room for anything but typography.
best_for: Charity / donation campaigns, creative-collective and type-foundry poster sites where type is the product — an oversized printed-poster register, one mint canvas, one black ink, type-as-architecture, Field Notes / It's Nice That-adjacent.
name: Good Glyphs
palette_voice: Anti-UI two-color system: one soft Pledge Mint (#c7ffcd) canvas carries the entire chromatic load while pure Ink Black (#000000) handles every stroke, border, label, and filled element — no neutral grays, no semantic colors, no shadows, no gradients; the only color-on-color moment is mint glyph artwork on the black showcase band; surfaces alternate between full-bleed mint and full-bleed black bands for a poster-strip rhythm instead of card hierarchy.
signature_moves: 288px / weight 300 / line-height 0.80 / -0.03em tracking display headline — the brand name rendered as a locked wall of ink, size IS the identity
Full-bleed mint-to-black band alternation producing poster-strip rhythm rather than card-based hierarchy
Fully pill-shaped 140px controls for every interactive element — no squared or rounded-rect variants, hover inverts fill (mint→black, black→mint)
Black showcase band spanning viewport width with 288px dingbat glyphs in Pledge Mint — the product proven at use size, the only color-on-black moment
1px solid black borders + 14px soft card radius — components feel stamped rather than designed

source.shadow: none — no elevation, hierarchy via scale and band alternation only

tagline: oversized charity poster on mint paper — type so large it behaves as architecture, not text.
typographic_voice: Helvetica Neue (subst. Inter/Neue Haas) at weight 300 powers the 288px display — the light weight at extreme size with locked -0.03em tracking lets the letters breathe inside a wall of ink, and the 0.80 line-height stacks them into a single graphic block; weight 400 handles all body/labels at 13-14px with the same tracking; one 28px mid-tier subhead jumps straight to 288px — never weight 700, type as architecture, not text.
